rule_1.name: interleave_step_parity
rule_1.description: Interweave main and vice; odd experiment steps lead with main, even steps lead with vice.

rule_1.name: interleave_main_vice
rule_1.description: Alternate characters from main and vice: main[i] then vice[i], truncated to ten characters.

rule_1.name: interleave_vice_main
rule_1.description: Alternate characters from vice and main: vice[i] then main[i].

rule_2.name: reverse_shift_concat
rule_2.description: Reverse current, shift all letters forward by the experiment step number modulo 26, then concatenate shifted_reverse + shifted_current.

rule_2.name: add_main_vice
rule_2.description: Add alphabet indices position-wise, A=0, returning chr(A + main[i] + vice[i]).

rule_3.name: append_step_char_copy
rule_3.description: Let a = step_number mod 10, using 10 when the remainder is 0; append current[a-1] repeated a times when available.

rule_3.name: dedupe_consecutive
rule_3.description: Remove consecutive duplicate characters from current.

rule_3.name: poswise_max
rule_3.description: Take the lexicographically larger character at each main/vice position.

rule_3.name: poswise_min
rule_3.description: Take the lexicographically smaller character at each main/vice position.

rule_4.name: previous_main_sum_prefix
rule_4.description: Use the previous experiment's main sequence: add alphabet indices of the first five current chars and previous_main position-wise modulo 26, then append the unchanged remainder.

rule_4.name: append_length_char
rule_4.description: Append the current sequence length encoded as A=1, B=2, ... when length is at most 26.

rule_4.name: poswise_max_rule4
rule_4.description: For each position, take main[i] if main[i] >= vice[i], otherwise take vice[i].

rule_5.name: prime_frequency_replace
rule_5.description: On prime-numbered experiment steps, replace every occurrence of the most frequent current letter with its next alphabet letter; otherwise leave current unchanged.

rule_5.name: sort_main_vice
rule_5.description: Combine main and vice strings then sort alphabetically, or sort current string if no main/vice.

induction.report:
rule_1: Interweave main and vice characters completely. The leading sequence is determined by the parity of current step number: main leads if odd, vice leads if even. Equivalent wording: alternating main and vice characters; merge main and vice with step-based leading character
rule_2: Reverse the current sequence and shift all characters forward by n, where n = current step number, positions in the alphabet cyclic A to B to ... to Z to A. Concatenate this with the similarly shifted version of the original sequence
rule_3: Select the character at position current step number mod 10, with 0 treated as 10. Copy this character a times, where a is that current step number modulo 10 value. Append the copies to the current sequence
rule_4: Take the first 5 characters of the current sequence and combine them character-wise with the last main sequence by adding their alphabet positions modulo 26. Append unchanged remainder of the current sequence after position 5
rule_5: If current step number is prime, find the most frequent letter in the current sequence and replace all its occurrences with the next letter in the alphabet cyclic A to B to ... to Z to A. Otherwise leave the sequence unchanged. This is replacing the most common character with its next letter on prime steps, a frequency-based substitution of the most frequent character when the step is prime
